items.title: Akiyoshi Toshiko — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: it was the [Chinese] Nationalist Army, Chiang Kai-shek‟s army, and they occupied the upstairs, too.

ctx.x: So after they ransacked your house, then what happened with your family?

Oh, just, we were fine, I was the only one who wasn‟t together [with them], except my oldest sister was married to a military man, so they were in China, they weren‟t there. Um … this was, as I said, it was 1946, uh…1945, excuse me, summer, and „til 1946 we were permitted, we left there, the first time it was occupied by Russians, then there was the Chinese communist army, and at that time they occupied … a lieutenant—actually his wife was also a lieutenant—they occupied our house‟s upstairs. And then after that,…
So what happened to your father‟s business?
